subject: Tenant connectivity readiness & routing handoff for Hearth Medical private deploy
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice@hearthmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@hearthmed.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment handoff — what we need from Redwood to validate routing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Our infra team will be doing the first pass at network / routing validation this week and asked me to collect the minimal handoff artifacts from Redwood so they can sign off on environment readiness. Can you confirm the list of items you need from us versus what Redwood will provide?

High-level items they mentioned:
- IP ranges/redwood egress/ingress expectations
- BGP/peering details (if applicable) or VPN endpoints
- Firewall / port lists and port directions (for both control plane and runtime lanes)
- SSH jump / bastion access for troubleshooting (temporary)
- Service account / certificate thumbprints and expected CNs for mutual TLS

We also have an internal compliance snapshot request for KMS/HSM integration details and audit-log retention expectations. We prefer to get this wrapped up by Fri 9/3 since the project kickoff is next Monday.

Appreciate any checklist or template you can share — if easier, an actionable to-do list we can check off would be ideal.

Thanks,
Alice
Infrastructure Manager
Hearth Medical

Hi Alice —

Thanks — good list. I put together a concise handoff checklist below and attached a small packet (redwood-onprem-prereqs.xlsx + network-diagram_v2.pdf). We can also do a 30m run-through with your ops team if useful.

Redwood -> We'll provide (deliverables):
- Public endpoints + expected egress IP ranges per region (see sheet: egress-ips)
- Control-plane FQDNs and mTLS certificate chain (CNs + thumbprints)
- Runtime endpoint port / protocol matrix (TCP ports, TLS, expected keepalives)
- Example BGP config (if you choose cross-connect) and static VPN endpoints (if not)
- A signed ARA (audit record access) snapshot for last 30 days and retention policy notes
- Support escalation contacts and temporary jump-host account for the initial validation window

Customer -> We'll need from Hearth:
- Tenant VPC CIDR and a list of subnets to be used for runtime vs control-plane peering
- Preferred connectivity mode: VPN or Direct Connect / cloud interconnect (include bandwidth targets)
- Any egress NAT gateway details and firewall-change window ownership
- SSH public keys for ops agents who will access the temporary Bastion (CSV preferred)
- KMS key material details / KMS policy contact for sealing keys (if you host keys)

Operational checks to validate during the handoff (these are the runbook checks):
1) Control-plane reachability: resolve FQDNs and validate TLS chain + CNs
2) Runtime Happy Path: request/response latency tests to sample endpoints across subnets
3) KV cache warming smoke test with a 1K token sequence to validate runtime memory config
4) BGP/route propagation: verify announced prefixes and route preferences match expected (AS path)
5) Log collection: validate log-forwarder endpoint accepts events and sample retention TTL

I'll loop Kim and Ben to coordinate the run-through and collect the ssh keys.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Marissa mobile: +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood-onprem-prereqs.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-diagram_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: alice@hearthmed.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment handoff — what we need from Redwood to validate routing

Marissa / Ben — quick technical notes to add before we formalize the runbook:

- Ports: runtime accepts outbound TLS 443 and inbound TLS 8443 for admin API (if customer exposes), plus ephemeral gRPC ports 10000-10010 for intra-cluster comms. Add those to the port matrix.
- MTLS: Redwood will provide the client cert for the control-plane; customer should trust the supplied root CA for the duration of the validation window. We rotate certs on a quarterly cadence.
- Bastion: we prefer ephemeral SSH keys (user-supplied) with a 7-day TTL we enforce on our side; ask Hearth if they can provide a short maintenance window for SSH access.
- BGP: if using direct-cloud interconnect, we will hand over AS preﬁx suggestions; make sure their peering ACLs allow BFD <-> keepalive timers (we recommend 3s/1s detection for rapid failover).

I also attached a small csv (connectivity-ssh-keys.csv) template we ask customers to fill for the initial set of ops keys.

I'll be on the run-through Fri 9/3 10:00-10:30 PT.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: connectivity-ssh-keys.csv (csv)
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment handoff — what we need from Redwood to validate routing

Hi Alice — thanks for pulling this together. A few operational notes from the Dedicated/private ops side:

- Maintenance window: to perform the initial routing and BGP validation we request a 1-hour window where your egress firewall rules can be updated. We don't need permanent changes — temporary allow rules are fine.
- Monitoring hooks: provide a Prometheus push gateway or a short-lived metrics ingestion endpoint we can use to confirm telemetry flow (we'll stop sending after the smoke tests).
- Audit/Logs: we will ship a sample syslog.gz with the first 72 hours of activity post-validation to your S3 bucket (need a write role).

Proposed next step: Marissa — can you send a calendar invite for the Fri 9/3 10:00 PT run-through and attach the latest deck and the sheet from the Drive link? Alice — if you can drop the ssh key csv and preferred connectivity mode by EOD, we can lock the checklist.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Deployment Operations, Redwood Inference
